title: 3DMapMaker Next — research references
note: Every entry is a real, publicly documented source that influenced a specific decision in this repository. The `usedFor` field names the file or package the decision landed in, so a reader can trace a claim back to the reason for it. Entries marked `verified: local` were read from files inside this repository rather than fetched from the network; the sandbox has no route to most CDNs, which is itself recorded in `blockedSources`.

references.title: Equirectangular projection
references.usedFor: packages/panorama/src/panorama.ts — directionToEquirectUv / equirectUvToDirection. A 2:1 equirect plate maps longitude linearly to u and latitude linearly to v.

references.title: 360° photography — equirectangular vs cubemap
references.usedFor: The decision to render an inverted sphere from a single equirect image rather than a cube map, per the brief's 'spherical never cube'.

references.title: Sphere geometry
references.usedFor: packages/scene-core/src/panoramaView.ts — the sphere segment counts (96 lon × 64 lat) and the geometry.scale(-1,1,1) inversion that puts the camera inside.

references.title: regl-based 360 viewer (camera at centre, distance 0)
references.usedFor: Confirmed the inverted-sphere approach and that the camera sits at the sphere centre with distance 0. 13 MB of working reference code audited locally.

references.title: Legacy reveal-space drag math and the no-cube constraint
references.usedFor: The drag-to-look mapping, the 'curved image, no cube, no black background' constraint, and the rule that WASD must never fire while a text field has focus.

references.title: Pole distortion in equirectangular panoramas
references.usedFor: packages/panorama/src/panorama.ts — analyzePoleValidity and the cap-blend shader, which fade the poles to sky/ground colour instead of smearing a single row of pixels.

references.title: Crossfade vs hard cut in image transitions
references.usedFor: PanoramaCrossfade.setProgress with persistenceEnabled=false does a hard cut at t=0.5 — two street plates ghosting together is worse than a clean swap.

references.title: Web Mercator (EPSG:3857)
references.usedFor: packages/gis — the projection used for any lat/lon to planar mapping in the project.

references.title: East-North-Up (ENU) local coordinate frame
references.usedFor: packages/gis — enuToScene / sceneToEnu. The Vec3 convention here is {x, y, z} with z as elevation, which is a frequent source of bugs and is asserted by coordinates.test.ts.

references.title: Haversine formula
references.usedFor: packages/gis — measureLocal for long baselines where a flat approximation would drift.

references.title: Great-circle distance
references.usedFor: packages/gis — polylineLength accumulation.

references.title: Shoelace formula for polygon area
references.usedFor: packages/gis — ringArea and ringPerimeter.

references.title: GeoJSON (RFC 7946)
references.usedFor: apps/web/src/state/io.ts — the GeoJSON export shape and the [lon, lat] ordering, which is the opposite of most internal conventions.

references.title: Port Harcourt coordinates
references.usedFor: apps/web/src/worlds/generate.ts — the world origin (4.8156°N, 7.0498°E) so the three demo worlds sit on real ground.

references.title: Quadtree
references.usedFor: packages/performance — the LodNode tree that selectLod walks.

references.title: Level of detail (computer graphics)
references.usedFor: packages/performance — selectLod(node, camera, opts, currentlyRefined) and the hysteresis that stops tiles flickering at a boundary.

references.title: Fractional Brownian motion
references.usedFor: packages/terrain/src/noise.ts — fbm(). This is where the real amplitude-cancelling bug was found: normalising by the sum of amplitudes made every terrain return 0–1 regardless of requested relief.

references.title: Perlin noise
references.usedFor: packages/terrain/src/noise.ts — the gradient lattice under the fbm octaves.

references.title: Simplex noise
references.usedFor: Considered and rejected for the heightfield: 2D Perlin is cheaper and the terrain is sampled on a regular grid, which removes simplex's main advantage.

references.title: Contour line extraction (marching squares)
references.usedFor: packages/terrain — extractContours(hf, interval, indexEvery, maxSegments) returning {segments, levels, bounds}.

references.title: Terrain skirt / crack-free chunk joining
references.usedFor: packages/terrain/src/mesh.ts — buildTerrainMesh skirt. The vertex buffer was undersized by 8(r−1) vertices, truncating exactly the ring the skirt exists to hide.

references.title: Digital elevation model
references.usedFor: The TerrainSource union in packages/project — why a heightfield carries resolution, size and origin rather than a bare array.

references.title: GeoTIFF
references.usedFor: The geotiff manual chunk in apps/web/vite.config.ts — kept out of the main bundle because nothing on the default path needs it.

references.title: Web Workers
references.usedFor: workers/terrain.worker.ts and TerrainWorkerClient — heightfield generation and contour extraction never run on the main thread.

references.title: Transferable objects and structured clone
references.usedFor: workers/terrain.worker.ts — Float32Array buffers are transferred rather than copied, so a 1024² heightfield does not double in memory on the way back.

references.title: Vertical exaggeration in terrain visualisation
references.usedFor: buildTerrainMesh verticalExaggeration — applied to the mesh only, never written back to the heightfield, so measurements stay true.

references.title: A* search algorithm
references.usedFor: packages/panorama/src/world-graph.ts — findPath. Reports `expanded` so the cost is visible rather than hidden.

references.title: Chebyshev distance
references.usedFor: The A* heuristic h = max(|dx|,|dy|) and the `nearby` spatial metric. A Euclidean disc would disagree with what a king-move walker can actually reach in N steps.

references.title: Chess — the king's move
references.usedFor: kingMovesFrom — the MAXIMUM possible moves (|dx|<=1, |dy|<=1, not both zero). A corner square has 3, an edge 5, an interior 8; this is correct, not a bug.

references.title: Admissible heuristic
references.usedFor: Chebyshev never overestimates a king-move path, so A* stays optimal. Using Euclidean here would be admissible but weaker; using Manhattan would be inadmissible and could return a suboptimal route.

references.title: Spatial hashing
references.usedFor: WorldGraph.nearby — a hash keyed by floor(g/cellSize) so a 1,024-node world answers a radius query without scanning the board.

references.title: Breadth-first search
references.usedFor: apps/web/src/worlds/frontier.ts — runFrontier grows outward from the start so the world is coherent around the reachable region even if generation is stopped part way.

references.title: Graph connectivity
references.usedFor: WorldGraph.isConnected — asserts the whole generated world is one component, so an unreachable destination is a real property and not a generator bug.

references.title: Adjacency list representation
references.usedFor: WorldGraph stores directed edges per node, which is what makes `connect` bidirectional-by-derivation and `neighbor(id, dir)` an O(degree) lookup.

references.title: Vite
references.usedFor: apps/web/vite.config.ts. Chosen over webpack for the dev-server speed and first-class worker imports. The authoritative config must live in apps/web, not the root — `npm run dev -w @3dmm/web` sets cwd to apps/web.

references.title: Vite server.allowedHosts
references.usedFor: allowedHosts: true, without which the preview host returns 403 and the app looks broken for a reason that has nothing to do with the code.

references.title: Vite build.rollupOptions.manualChunks
references.usedFor: Splitting three (529 kB) and geotiff out of the main bundle.

references.title: npm workspaces
references.usedFor: The apps/* + packages/* monorepo layout in the root package.json, which is what replaces the monolithic single-file architecture.

references.title: ResizeObserver
references.usedFor: apps/web/src/ui/WorldMap.tsx and WorldView.tsx — the map and the renderer resize with their panel, which is what keeps the viewport interactive in fullscreen. The legacy app captured one static frame instead.

references.title: Pointer Events and setPointerCapture
references.usedFor: WorldMap and WorldView drag handling. Per-element capture is what stops dragging the UI from rotating the camera — the legacy app used one global document mousemove with a shared isDragging flag.

references.title: requestAnimationFrame
references.usedFor: The WorldView render loop and the gait integrator. Delta time is clamped to 0.1 s so a backgrounded tab does not teleport the transition on return.

references.title: createImageBitmap
references.usedFor: apps/web/src/worlds/preloader.ts — decodes a plate off the main thread. Budgeted on width*height*4 because the decoded RGBA is what actually costs memory, not the compressed file.

references.title: AbortController / AbortSignal
references.usedFor: Every async job in the app. Two separate controllers in worldSession — one for the walk, one for the prefetch batch — because sharing them made a walk cancel the very fetch it needed.

references.title: Hash-based routing for static builds
references.usedFor: apps/web/src/App.tsx — #/, #/editor, #/tutorial, #/qa, #/worlds. Works from any host or file path with no server rewrite rules.

references.title: URL.createObjectURL
references.usedFor: The fallback decode path in preloader.ts when createImageBitmap is unavailable. Absent in jsdom, so the tests stub it explicitly.

references.title: Blob and Blob.size
references.usedFor: preloader.ts — the compressed size half of the cache's byte accounting.

references.title: three.js
references.usedFor: packages/scene-core. Chosen over regl for the scene graph, material system and loader ecosystem; the legacy reference viewer used regl directly.

references.title: three.js ShaderMaterial and uniforms
references.usedFor: packages/scene-core/src/panoramaView.ts — uMap, uOpacity, uCapsEnabled, uExposure, uVFovScale. Opacity as a uniform is what makes an interrupted crossfade exact rather than approximate.

references.title: three.js ColorManagement and SRGBColorSpace
references.usedFor: renderer.outputColorSpace and texture.colorSpace in WorldView — without both, plates render washed out.

references.title: Texture disposal and GPU memory
references.usedFor: The crossfade texture-ownership fix. setTexture used to dispose whatever it replaced; during a fade the two spheres share the outgoing texture, so the second walk disposed the plate still on screen.

references.title: PerspectiveCamera field of view
references.usedFor: WorldView — V_FOV 78° with the horizontal FOV following the aspect ratio, so a wide window sees more of the plate rather than a stretched crop.

references.title: Row-major vs column-major matrices
references.usedFor: A note for future maintainers: the projection matrices in this repository are ROW-MAJOR throughout. three.js is column-major internally, so do not 'fix' one side.

references.title: Synchronous GPU readback stalls the pipeline
references.usedFor: Why the legacy applyPersistenceEffect (domElement.toDataURL on the default framebuffer) was replaced with a shader-side blend.

references.title: Frustum culling and renderOrder
references.usedFor: panoramaView.ts — frustumCulled = false and renderOrder = -1000 so the sky sphere is never culled when the camera sits at its centre.

references.title: zustand
references.usedFor: apps/web/src/state/store.ts. Chosen over Redux for the absence of boilerplate and over Context for selector-based re-render control.

references.title: zustand subscribeWithSelector middleware
references.usedFor: The store's cross-slice reactions, which need a subscription that fires only when a projected value actually changes.

references.title: Single source of truth
references.usedFor: The central rule of the panorama world: WorldGraph is authoritative, and both the 2D map and the 360° viewer derive from it. Neither holds a copy, so they cannot drift.

references.title: Finite-state machine
references.usedFor: The WorldSession transition machine: idle → preloading → transitioning → settling → idle. Explicit stages are what make 'no jarring black screen' a testable property rather than a hope.

references.title: Command pattern / undo stack
references.usedFor: packages/input — the command registry and bindings behind the command palette and the undo/redo history.

references.title: ECS and data-oriented design in the browser
references.usedFor: Considered for the scene and rejected: the editor's object counts are in the hundreds, not the tens of thousands, so a plain object graph with a zustand mirror is simpler and easier to inspect.

references.title: Schema versioning and migrations
references.usedFor: packages/project — schema v6 with explicit migration steps, and validateProject returning the repaired project rather than a boolean.

references.title: Defensive parsing of untrusted input
references.usedFor: apps/web/src/state/io.ts — sanitizeImportedJson. An imported project is untrusted input even when it came from this same app.

references.title: Radix UI primitives
references.usedFor: packages/ui — Popover, Tooltip and friends, wrapped by the local Button/Slider/Segmented components. Unstyled primitives with correct focus and ARIA behaviour.

references.title: ARIA application role
references.usedFor: The map canvas and the panorama stage both use role="application" with a tabIndex, so a screen reader hands keystrokes to the widget instead of reading them as page content.

references.title: WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow
references.usedFor: The no-page-level-horizontal-overflow rule. worldMap.test.tsx asserts the SVG is width/height 100% rather than the board's pixel size.

references.title: Keyboard focus management
references.usedFor: WorldView.onKeyDown refuses WASD while an input/textarea/select has focus. The legacy app gated on activeElement === renderer.domElement and never cleared keys on blur, so movement stuck.

references.title: prefers-reduced-motion
references.usedFor: The map's pulsing current-node ring is a CSS/SMIL animation that a reduced-motion user can have suppressed; it carries no information the static state does not.

references.title: SVG accessibility and text alternatives
references.usedFor: The map's aria-label states the board dimensions and node count, and the legend names all seven node states, so the map is not purely visual.

references.title: Seeded pseudorandom number generators
references.usedFor: generateWorld(spec) — a seed produces a byte-identical graph, asserted by comparing toJSON() across two runs.

references.title: Box–Muller transform
references.usedFor: GaussianRng in packages/panorama/src/grid.ts. Confined to camera bob, micro yaw/pitch and timing jitter — never to node selection, coordinates, geometry or path correctness.

references.title: Wave Function Collapse
references.usedFor: Considered for the world layout and rejected: the graph needs hard guarantees (every edge geometrically true, one connected component) that a constraint solver over tiles would make harder to assert.

references.title: Procedural city generation
references.usedFor: apps/web/src/worlds/generate.ts — a spine road that dog-legs rather than running straight diagonal, cross streets, a river with crossings on the larger worlds, and building clusters that remove cells entirely.

references.title: Deterministic simulation and replay
references.usedFor: Why intent resolution is asserted identical over 200 runs: if the RNG could reach a movement decision, the world would not be reproducible.

references.title: Google Maps Platform Terms — Street View imagery
references.usedFor: The hard rule in frontier.ts: reference geography only, never scrape or redistribute imagery. The continuity gate rejects a provenance source matching googleapis, maps/api or streetview.

references.title: Google Street View metadata API (geographic reference only)
references.usedFor: Confirms the split between metadata (allowed as geographic reference) and the pixel data (not redistributed). The generated layer and the reference layer are kept separate in WorldNode.provenance.

references.title: OpenStreetMap — attribution requirements
references.usedFor: The accepted form of a reference source: a named attribution, not a fetch endpoint. frontier.test.ts asserts this exact distinction both ways.

references.title: Creative Commons licences
references.usedFor: The provenance.license field on every generated node. A plate with no licence is rejected by the continuity gate.

references.title: Provenance metadata for generated media
references.usedFor: WorldNode.provenance — sourceType, referenceSources, generator, createdAt, license. Every plate carries it; nothing is unattributed.

references.title: Vitest
references.usedFor: The test runner. Chosen because it shares the Vite config, so the same aliases and worker handling that the app uses apply to the tests.

references.title: Testing Library — query by role and test id
references.usedFor: apps/web/src/ui/__tests__/worldMap.test.tsx — getByRole('application') and getByTestId, so the tests break when the accessible surface changes, not when markup is restyled.

references.title: jsdom limitations for canvas and WebGL
references.usedFor: vitest.setup.ts shims ResizeObserver and getContext('2d'); WebGL returns null. This is what makes the error-path test possible, and it is why no visual render is claimed.

references.title: Playwright
references.usedFor: The intended E2E runner. Version 1.63.0 is installed but the browser binaries cannot be downloaded in this sandbox, so no E2E test has passed and none is claimed.

references.title: Property-based testing
references.usedFor: The invariant style used across generate.test.ts and world-graph.test.ts: assert the property (every edge matches its delta; adjacency is reciprocal) rather than a snapshot of one layout.

references.title: Regression testing
references.usedFor: Each of the ten bugs in DEVELOPMENT_LOG.md §5 now has a test that fails if the bug returns — including the ones whose original test passed for the wrong reason.

references.title: Round-trip (invertibility) testing
references.usedFor: mapModel.test.ts — gridToScreen then screenToGrid returns the original cell for all 64 cells of the small board and sampled cells of the 32×32 board.

references.title: Least-recently-used cache eviction
references.usedFor: apps/web/src/worlds/preloader.ts — a JS Map, whose insertion order is kept current by delete-then-set on read, gives O(1) LRU with no extra structure.

references.title: Prefetching and cache locality
references.usedFor: rankPrefetch — facing direction first, then the rest of the ring, then the route. Cached plates are skipped so the queue is honest about what will actually be fetched.

references.title: Request deduplication / single-flight
references.usedFor: PanoramaCache.load collapses concurrent requests for one url. The subtlety found here: the deduped caller must not inherit the first caller's abort signal.

references.title: Viewport culling
references.usedFor: mapModel.ts — boards over 400 nodes render only the viewport plus a margin, and report how many were culled so 'n of m nodes' is not a guess.

references.title: Main-thread budget and jank
references.usedFor: The rule that terrain generation runs in a worker, contour extraction is capped by maxSegments, and the frontier pipeline is cancellable and capped by maxCells.

references.title: Typed arrays and typed-array writes past the end
references.usedFor: The terrain skirt bug: writing past the end of a Float32Array is silent, not an exception, which is why the truncated ring went unnoticed.

references.title: Code splitting and dynamic import
references.usedFor: The manualChunks split that keeps three and geotiff out of the initial payload.

references.title: The Rust Programming Language
references.usedFor: The native terrain core. rustc 1.88.0 is installed at /home/user/.rusttoolchain and a native build plus a wasm32 cdylib build were both verified.

references.title: wasm32-unknown-unknown target and cdylib crate type
references.usedFor: The zero-dependency cdylib decision. crates.io is unreachable from this sandbox, so wasm-bindgen is not available and the JS glue is hand-written.

references.title: WebAssembly JavaScript API
references.usedFor: The hand-written instantiation glue, verified end to end with add(20,22)=42, and the TypeScript path kept as the fallback.

references.title: @rustbin scope — Rust components as npm tarballs
references.usedFor: The only working route to a Rust toolchain here. jsdelivr, unpkg, crates.io, deb.debian.org and static.rust-lang.org were all unreachable.

references.title: Tauri
references.usedFor: The intended desktop shell for the Rust core. Not built here: the deliverable is web-only, and the crate workspace is not yet populated.

references.title: Yaw, pitch and roll
references.usedFor: The camera model. WorldView applies rotateY then rotateX from a zeroed rotation each frame, which is what keeps pitch from accumulating into roll.

references.title: Compass bearing and azimuth
references.usedFor: quantiseToDirection — 0° is north, clockwise. The eight compass points are the quantisation targets for a camera-relative keypress.

references.title: Camera-relative movement
references.usedFor: packages/panorama/src/intent.ts — key + cameraYaw → world heading → nearest compass direction → graph edge. The same key reaches three different nodes depending on where the camera faces.

references.title: Shortest-arc angle interpolation
references.usedFor: lerpAngle in WorldView — wrapping ((to-from+540)%360)-180 so easing from 350° to 10° goes the 20° way round, not the 340° way.

references.title: Input buffering for responsive controls
references.usedFor: WorldSession.pending — a keypress during a transition is queued (up to 3) and replayed on arrival rather than dropped, so fast walking does not lose input.

references.title: Procedural camera shake and motion noise
references.usedFor: The gait struct. Small-sigma noise on bob, yaw and pitch only; the struct carries no coordinates or node ids, which is asserted directly.

references.title: Walking gait and vertical displacement
references.usedFor: packages/panorama/src/grid.ts — the ~1.85 Hz bob frequency and the integrated sway, chosen so the walk reads as a person moving rather than a floating camera.

references.title: Exposure value and relative brightness
references.usedFor: exposureRatio in packages/panorama and the exposure continuity check, which compares plates by log ratio so a doubling is a doubling at any brightness.

references.title: Solar azimuth angle
references.usedFor: isPlausibleSunTime in frontier.ts — the sun sweeps roughly 90° (east) to 270° (west) across the day, which is how the gate catches a noon sun stamped onto a dusk plate.

references.title: Panorama stitching seams
references.usedFor: The seam-continuity checks in frontier.ts: sun direction, exposure and weather are compared across every edge so adjacent plates do not visibly disagree.

references.title: Scale factor and map distance
references.usedFor: The metersPerGridUnit rule: a grid step is not a metre. Cardinal edges measure 25 m and diagonals 25√2 ≈ 35.4 m, asserted to be different.

references.title: ES modules and package exports
references.usedFor: Each package under packages/*/src with its own index barrel. A package.json `main` pointing at .ts when the file is .tsx will fail to resolve, which is a bug that was hit and fixed here.

references.title: glTF 2.0
references.usedFor: packages/assets — loadModel(file, name, opts) returning {scene, analysis, bytes}, the format chosen for authored 3D models.

references.title: Heightfield / heightmap terrain
references.usedFor: Heightfield(resolution, size, originX, originY, data?) with .sample(), .minMax(), .applyEdits() and .toEdits() — the sculpt tools write edits, not raw heights, so they stay undoable.

references.title: Test doubles — stubs and spies
references.usedFor: preloader.test.ts and worldSession.test.ts stub fetch, Image and createImageBitmap to drive the real PanoramaCache and WorldSession through their failure and abort paths.

references.title: Memory budgeting for decoded image data
references.usedFor: The cache budgets on width*height*4 rather than the JPEG file size. A 1456×720 plate is ~4.2 MB decoded against ~260 kB on disk, a 16× difference that would have blown any file-size budget.

references.title: Autosave and crash recovery
references.usedFor: The store's autosave with recoveryWarnings surfaced once as a visible notice rather than applied silently.

references.title: Command palette pattern
references.usedFor: apps/web/src/ui/CommandPalette.tsx over the packages/input command registry, so the palette and the keyboard bindings cannot disagree.

references.title: Pitch clamping in first-person views
references.usedFor: WorldView PITCH_LIMIT of 62°, so the player can never look past the poles where an equirect plate degenerates to a single row.

references.title: Content Security Policy and no inline script
references.usedFor: The module-only architecture. The legacy 183 KB single-file app was fundamentally incompatible with a strict CSP; the new app is not.

references.title: Honest reporting of unverified claims
references.usedFor: DEVELOPMENT_LOG.md §3 states plainly that the browser binary is unavailable, that jsdom tests are not browser tests, and that the 360° viewer's pixels are unconfirmed. No E2E pass is claimed.

references.title: Landmark-based navigation and cognitive maps
references.usedFor: Landmark carries a persistent id and WorldGraph.landmarkVector returns {dx, dy, meters, bearingDeg}. Distance to the church shrinks monotonically along the route, asserted to reach 0.

references.title: Monotonic heuristic and route quality
references.usedFor: Why the recommended route can be shown without forcing it: A* with a consistent heuristic gives a stable shortest path, so re-planning after a detour converges rather than oscillating.

blockedSources.impact: Playwright browser binaries cannot be downloaded, so no E2E test has run.
No wasm-bindgen, so the Rust crate is a zero-dep cdylib with hand-written JS glue.
Direct rustup distribution blocked; the toolchain came from the @rustbin npm scope instead.
No live elevation or map tiles, so every demo world is fully procedural and local.
